「もの」（漢字（かんじ）では「物（もの）」）は、形式名詞（けいしきめいし）と呼（よ）ばれていて、名前（なまえ）がついていないものや、複雑（ふくざつ）でどう呼（よ）べばいいかわからないものを表（あらわ）すときなどに使（つか）われます。このような「もの」が助動詞（じょどうし）の「だ」に付（つ）くと、「(A) は一般常識（いっぱんじょうしき）だ」「(A) は当（あ）たり前（まえ）だ」「ふつうは (A) だ」のような意味（いみ）になります。これは、習慣（しゅうかん）や決（き）まり、常識（じょうしき）や、状況（じょうきょう）から見（み）てそうなるのが自然（しぜん）だと思（おも）われる結果（けっか）を表（あらわ）すときに使（つか）われます。

「ものだ」は、連体形（れんたいけい）の語の、あとに付（つ）けて使（つか）います。

「ものだ」は、否定（ひてい）の形（かたち）でも使（つか）われます。この場合（ばあい）は、「ものではない」や「ものじゃない」という形（かたち）になります。そして、「本来（ほんらい）は〜ではない」や「一般的（いっぱんてき）に〜すべきではない」のような意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

会話（かいわ）では、「もん」という短（みじか）い形（かたち）がよく使（つか）われます。これを使（つか）うと、くだけた印象（いんしょう）になります。
attributes.body:
もの (or 物（もの） in its kanji form) is classified as a 形式名詞（けいしきめいし） (dummy noun) in Japanese. This just means a noun that is used in a similar way to 'thing' in English. もの regularly refers to things that do not have their own name, or are difficult to name due to their complexity. When もの is combined with the auxiliary verb だ, it implies that the previously mentioned (A) is something that 'is what it is'. This is often used in relation to customs, conventions, common sense, or to highlight results that would naturally be expected in any given situation.

To use ものだ, attach it to the end of the attributive form of any word/word that ends a phrase that you would like to highlight as being an obvious piece of information.

ものだ as 'supposed to', or 'the way it is' can also be used to negate a phrase, and say that it is 'something that isn't expected', or 'shouldn't be the case'. To do this, だ will be replaced with ではない, or じゃない.

Caution

もの may sometimes be abbreviated as もん. This is far more common in spoken language, and can make the statement sound a bit more casual overall.

attributes.description: 接続・意味・使い方・例文

attributes.body: ものだ expresses general or societal expectations, e.g. 子どもは早く寝るものだ ('Children are supposed to go to bed early.') べきではない carries the opposite nuance, conveying that one should not do something based on moral or social reasoning, e.g. 人を見た目で判断すべきではない ('You shouldn't judge people by appearances.')

first_relatable.title: ものだ
first_relatable.meaning: Supposed to, Should, That's the way it is

second_relatable.title: べきではない
second_relatable.meaning: Should not, Must not , Ought not to

attributes.body: Both expressions use the same ものだ, with the only difference being the presence or absence of から 'because/since'. Therefore, ものだ is used at the end of a sentence to express the idea of how something is or should be. In contrast, ものだから presents a reason or an explanation for something, and is often used when justifying a certain action or situation. ものだ can also be used to express obligation, while ものだから is not used this way.

first_relatable.title: ものだ
first_relatable.meaning: Supposed to, Should, That's the way it is

attributes.body: While both expressions contain もの, they are used with very different nuances. ものですから・もので offers a reason, and is often used to explain or justify one's personal actions or situation, e.g. 忙しかったものですから 'I was busy, so...'. In contrast, ものだ is used to express a natural tendency or general truth, e.g. １２月は仕事が忙しいものです ('Work is busy in December.', implying that's just the way it is).

first_relatable.title: ものですから・もので
first_relatable.meaning: Because, My excuse is, My explanation is

second_relatable.title: ものだ
second_relatable.meaning: Supposed to, Should, That's the way it is

attributes.body: Both express what should be done, but with different nuance. ことだ is used to give firm advice, e.g. 諦めずに続けることだ ('You should keep going without giving up.') ものだ expresses general expectations or norms, e.g. 仕事は地道に頑張り続けるものだ ('One is expected to keep working steadily.')

second_relatable.title: ものだ
second_relatable.meaning: Supposed to, Should, That's the way it is

attributes.body: Both express what one 'should' do, but with different nuance. べき reflects personal or moral judgment, e.g. 約束は守るべきだ ('You should keep your promises.') ものだ conveys social or cultural expectations, e.g. 子どもは早く寝るものだ ('Children are supposed to go to bed early.')

first_relatable.title: ものだ
first_relatable.meaning: Supposed to, Should, That's the way it is

attributes.body: はずだ conveys a specific expectation or prediction based on current evidence, like 雨が降るはずだ ('It should rain.'). ものだ expresses a general rule or common tendency, like 雨は春によく降るものだ ('It often rains in spring.'). The former is situational, while the latter is habitual or cultural.

first_relatable.title: はずだ
first_relatable.meaning: Bound to (be), Expected to (be), Should be (able)

second_relatable.title: ものだ
second_relatable.meaning: Supposed to, Should, That's the way it is
